lines: Phases 1 to 5 complete. Phase 6 in progress. The decision asked of Brandon in Status 236 at about 5:20 PM MT Friday stands unanswered: move on to the film and the masters, or one more round of looks first. The work goes on in either case and only the freeze waits.

Chain 43 passed and is on the main branch since 8:42 PM MT Friday: the shutter's mend for flown pieces at the masters' tier (decisions 258 and 261). Measured by the chain's helper on the merged tree, its report read whole here: type check and build exit 0, engine 144059cb99b0d134 as expected, all eight guard stills equal to the list in force, so the page's stills are not changed, the cover at the swap in the four shakes 0.9694, 0.889, 0.9572 and 0.961, the scene seen after the settle 0.9932, 1, 0.99 and 0.9998, at most 1,774,148 of 1,800,000 triangles at high, the whole test run 1064 passed and 8 skipped in 72 files with 0 failed, three tests more than chain 42 and all three the mend's own. Measured here: those eight lines and the triangle gate's line are the same characters as chain 42's. The helper then drew film frames 681 and 682 at preview size at the masters' tier from the same tree (86 and 76 seconds, 24 samples each, stated by it). Looked at here whole and at three times: each flown petal is one smear, with no rib and no row of copies, and sandy at its edges when enlarged. That sand is open item 278 and stays open as decision 261 says, with no fourth mend without his word. The mend acts at the masters' tier, where the film is drawn (stated by its builder).

The frost line at film frame 668 (item 275). Decision 262. Its builder wrote that the main branch had moved twice under its proof and that a pair of pictures with spring's old glass on one side would be muddled. It draws every floor again on real heads and reports about 10:20 PM MT instead of about 9:20 PM MT. Ruled: taken. Its offer of a sooner report on the earlier main branch is not taken, since the merge needs the proof on the real head in any case. It was told ahead that chain 43 moves the main branch once more and that it does not draw again for that. Nothing is pushed by it yet (stated by it).

The stall at low quality. Decision 263. The one try stands as a local form: the bar's tints as whole 255ths and the menu's sheet the same bytes as the main branch's. Measured by its builder on a quiet machine, its compare file read here: 336 pictured states of the controls and all 336 the same in every pixel as the main branch's. Of 708 held pictures of the fades 694 are the same and 14 one level apart, which the main branch shows against itself too. The whole test run on its tree 1072 passed and 8 skipped. So floor 1 is met where it has always been measured. Its finding: on a machine starved on purpose, two states of the menu at phone size with a mouse differ from the main branch's by one level in 14 corner pixels, and one held fade by one level in 4 pixels, in 2 of 2 starved runs of the mend and 0 of 2 of the main branch. Cause not found. Seen here in its pictures: nothing at the menu's own size. Ruled: this does not hold the push. It is open item 284, not mended, and no further try is given, since a further change would put the 336 equal states at risk. Its push is due about 9:15 PM MT and its last floor about 9:55 PM MT. Not seen by anyone: a real graphics card.

The Direct3D mend. Stated by the render instructions' builder from a hosted Windows machine without a graphics card (Chrome 158 through Direct3D 11, the film page at 960x540, 13 frames), the second and last list for the mend's branch: the warning on the tests for a broken number is gone, the warning on a read inside a loop is gone, and the caution on a value that may not be set stays in one place only, fall's leaf cards in 1 program, which decision 259 leaves on purpose (open item 282). One more message, not new: one program's optimization does not converge, the one with summer's glass. 114 programs linked, 0 errors. The mender's whole report is due about 9:11 PM MT, with the answer whether Windows through Direct3D 11 draws fall's leaves with their veins.

The final render on his own computer. Stated by its builder of its newer hosted run: Windows with Git Bash passed in 23 minutes, with PowerShell in 31, with the newest long term Node in 36, the install lines in 7, macOS at 3840 in 14 and the send back test in 1. The small macOS job failed a second time because Chrome updated itself on the hosted machine between the short test and the render. The proof now follows the file's own row for that case, test again and render again, and when the test after an update fails the render line is not run and the tool refuses it. The two Windows jobs at 3840x2160 were still drawing after 45 minutes on a software card, and their numbers are the last the floors need. No final render is started in the cloud.

Remaining in phase 6 and what he receives. Chain 44: the stall's mend (push due about 9:15 PM MT), the Direct3D mend (report due about 9:11 PM MT), summer's fireflies and the seeds' dots (first report now due by 9:25 PM MT and the second by 10:50 PM MT, since its builder draws its guards again on the new main branch), the frost line at film frame 668 (report due about 10:20 PM MT), as each passes. Then a critic for the change of season and a fifteenth publish. The render instructions: one file in the repo and one line to give Claude Code, then a cold read by a fresh critic. On his word the freeze: the repo goes private and the references are redrawn. Then the film steps of the build order and the full 4K 60 render on his gaming PC on his word: With Prompt and Without Prompt at 3840x2160, the Portfolio Looping Video and the Portfolio Screenshot. Last, a fresh reviewer's score against the showcase standard.

Open, below the bar: summer's landing streaks whiter and coarser than approved and its base darker. Summer's pond at rest (item 279). Fall's storm paler than approved. Spring's glass after a shake pale on pale, with square corners at the lower ends of a few runs. Spring's fence and trails. The fireflies' flat bars at 4K (item 276). The seeds' lumps of dots at the stills' close camera (item 277). The sand of the petals' mend at 4K before the encode, one small petal's softer edge and the petals' fringe at film frames 681 and 682 (item 278). The frost line at film frame 668 (item 275). The stall at low quality on a software renderer, until chain 44. One compiler caution on Windows at fall's leaf cards (item 282). The square pressed fill of one menu option (item 283). One level in 14 corner pixels of the menu on a starved machine (item 284). Winter's four small items. Fall's near fence and the pumpkin's stepped face (item 272). The poster tool that stops on one failed request (item 273).
Sound credits 7,420 of 10,000 (measured from the ledger: 52 calls), no call since 05:47 UTC on Thursday (10:47 PM MT Wednesday). No film render and no new preview since Preview 07.

allowance (after the review): 48.95 h used of 12.00 h allowed
